new_jobs.title: Data Scientist II
new_jobs.description:
At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for equity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Data Scientist II
to help us fulfill that mission.

ACT is seeking a Data Scientist II to help build a new pathway navigation experience that helps high school students explore, plan, and take confident next steps toward college and career. This role will design, test, and validate the data models that power personalized college, career, and pathway recommendations. You will work cross-functionally with product, engineering, research, design, and business partners to combine student, education, assessment, interest, skills, and career data into relevant, explainable, and actionable recommendations. You will move quickly from early experimentation to production implementation while ensuring that models are accurate, transparent, fair, and appropriate for use with students and families.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $95,000 to $105,000.
ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity.

Location:
This is a remote position, based in the United States.
Visa:
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

Please Note: This is a Fixed Term Position that will last 6 months, with the possibility of an extension.

What You Will Be Working On

Data Science and AI Development:

Design, prototype, and evaluate models that generate personalized college, career, and pathway recommendations
Apply statistical modeling, machine learning, and generative AI to rapidly test and improve product capabilities
Evaluate model performance, fairness, bias, and appropriate use

Product Data And Experimentation

Design data collection strategies that capture student behavior, performance, and engagement while supporting rapid product development
Analyze pilot and user-study data and translate findings into actionable product recommendations
Define metrics and experiments to evaluate recommendation quality and product impact

Data Architecture And Production

Partner with engineers to build scalable cloud-based data pipelines and move models from prototype into production
Integrate data from student, education, assessment, skills, career, and labor-market sources
Establish reliable processes for data security, model documentation, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance

Student-Centered Personalization

Develop approaches that produce useful recommendations when student data is incomplete and adapt as new information becomes available
Use behavioral and performance data to support personalized and adaptive product experiences
Make model outputs understandable and actionable for various stakeholders

Cross-Organizational Collaboration

Collaborate across teams to align data, modeling, research, and product requirements
Translate research and business needs into data collection plans and technical solutions
Communicate analytical findings, assumptions, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

Bachelor’s degree in data science, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics, economics, operations research, or a related quantitative discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired
At least 3 years of applied data science experience, including building statistical or machine-learning models and analyzing product experiments, pilots, or user studies
Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience developing scalable data pipelines and moving data products or models from prototype toward production

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

A hands-on, product-oriented data scientist who can move from analysis and rapid prototyping to production implementation
Strong in statistical modeling, machine learning, experimental design, and model evaluation
Experienced in scalable data pipelines, cloud environments, and integrating complex data sources
Skilled at using behavioral and performance data to develop personalized product experiences
Thoughtful about responsible AI, including fairness, bias mitigation, transparency, privacy, and appropriate use
An effective cross-functional communicator who translates research and business needs into actionable technical solutions

It’s a Plus If You Have (preferred Requirements)

Master’s degree in data science or related field
Experience with recommender systems, generative AI, natural language processing, or personalized and adaptive systems
Experience with education, assessment, career, workforce, labor-market, occupational, or skills data

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the Team

The Agentic Engineering organization at ServiceNow is the customer-obsessed engineering group that builds a conversational AI experience that turns enterprise intent into completed work. We advance how enterprise AI reasons, remembers, and executes.

The Agent Orchestration team — the team you'll join — owns the execution core: the agent harness, orchestration runtime, multi-agent coordination, memory management, and the evaluation frameworks that ensure agents behave correctly in production. Every autonomous action Otto promises depends on what this team ships.

By joining our team, you’ll be at the forefront of our AI transformation journey, backed by the global scale of ServiceNow and the agility of a high-growth environment. We are looking for world-class talent to help us extend agentic AI to every employee across every corner of the business

What You Get To Do In This Role

As a Staff AI Engineer, you will own significant parts of the agent harness — the infrastructure layer that enables AI agents to reason over real enterprise data, take action across workflows, and run safely at Fortune 500 scale.

Harness engineering: Design and build the agent execution harness — the orchestration layer that routes inputs, manages context, invokes tools, handles retries, and surfaces execution state across multi-step agentic workflows
Reliability at scale: Own the runtime's fault tolerance, latency, and throughput; design for enterprise workflows that cannot fail silently or unpredictably
Observability: Instrument the harness with tracing, cost attribution, and latency visibility so the team can reason about agent behavior in production and catch failures before customers do
Prompt infrastructure: Build prompt management systems — versioning, templating, and systematic evaluation — that keep agent behavior stable across model updates and configuration changes
Eval engineering: Design and own evaluation frameworks (unit evals, integration evals, production monitors) that measure agent quality, catch regressions, and drive data-informed decisions
LLM integration: Integrate with and abstract over frontier LLMs, managing model routing, fallback strategies, cost, and latency trade - offs in production
Technical leadership: Set technical standards through architecture decisions, code reviews, and coaching — particularly on agentic design patterns and production AI discipline.
System boundary design: Define where agent logic lives — what's a tool call, a sub-agent, a hardcoded path, or a human escalation — and establish those design standards across the team

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

7+ years building production software systems with a strong track record on reliability, performance, and scalability
Hands-on experience shipping generative AI products — not just integrating LLM APIs or building prototypes, but owning AI-powered features that production users depend on
Solid depth in how large language models work: failure modes, context constraints, and how prompt design shapes model behavior at scale
Practical prompt engineering experience: systematically designing, versioning, and evaluating prompts across model updates or A/B evaluation cycles
A real track record in eval engineering — not just familiarity, but a portfolio of evaluation suites designed, shipped, and used to drive quality decisions in production AI systems
Cost and efficiency awareness at the system level: experience reasoning about model routing, inference cost, and latency tradeoffs in production
Strong software engineering fundamentals: distributed systems, API design, and testing discipline
Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous, startup-like AI product environments

Nice to Have

Experience with multi-agent coordination patterns (A2A, MCP)
Familiarity with agent frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar)
Prior experience shipping AI systems in enterprise software
Experience with AI observability tooling (tracing, cost tracking, LLM-specific monitoring)
Familiarity with cloud-native infrastructure, service observability, logging, monitoring, reliability engineering, and production troubleshooting

, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. new_jobs.title: ML Engineer & Research Scientist, Speech (Full-time)
new_jobs.description:
ML Engineer & Research Scientist, Speech (Full-time)
Location: San Francisco · Type: Full-time 

About Voice Arena
Voice Arena builds frontier evals, models and datasets for voice AI. Our mission is to make machines talk like humans, and to measure honestly how close they are.
We run public leaderboards for speech to text, text to speech, speech to speech and speaker diarization, with many more yet to come. Labs, voice platforms and enterprises use them to see how speech models perform on real speech, in real conditions and across languages, rather than on clean read audio.
Behind the boards is a research and engineering team that builds its own datasets, trains the models that keep its evaluations accurate and publishes its methods. What sets us apart:
Research that gets published.
Three papers at Interspeech 2026, where Voice Arena is also the Diamond Sponsor. Our methods go through peer review, not just a blog post.
Partners across the field.
We brought Hindi and Indian English to Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard, and we partner with NVIDIA. Model providers send us new models for public and private evaluation.
Data nobody else has.
Monsoon, our dataset initiative for the Global South, is working towards 1,000 languages by 2027. Our accented English corpus covers 8 accents and 6,000 hours. This data gives us held-out test sets that models have not seen in training.
A research community.
Voice Research Club runs paper-first sessions for voice AI researchers, starting in San Francisco and New York, with more cities to follow.

About the role
Our mission is to make machines talk like humans. Before that is an engineering problem, it is a research problem: someone has to define what talking like a human actually means, measure how far today's models are from it, and show what closes the gap.
We're hiring an ML Engineer & Research Scientist to own that problem end to end. This role blends fundamental research and hands-on engineering, and we don't separate the two. You will decide which behaviours the best voice models should have, build the evals that measure them, define the data that teaches them, and train the models that prove it works on our leaderboards and others.
The core question for this role is simple: what does a speech model need to do to talk like a human, and how do we prove when it does?
This is a highly autonomous role. You'll work directly with the founders in a small, talent-dense team, with real ownership from day one. Everything you ship is public. When a new speech model launches, labs and enterprises check our boards to see where it stands, so your evals decide what gets measured and your models show the field what is possible.

In this role, you will
The work is one end-to-end research loop. You'll run it again and again, each time on a different open problem in speech:
Identify the problems in speech.
Find the gaps between today's speech models and machines that talk like humans, across recognition, synthesis, turn-taking, conversation, emotion, languages and accents. Listen to where models fail, read the literature, talk to the labs and users who hit these failures every day, and turn what you find into clear problem statements.
Define the behaviour we want models to have.
For each problem, write down precisely how a model should behave: what a good response sounds like, what counts as a failure, and where the line between them sits. This becomes the target labs build towards.
Design the evals.
Turn that behaviour into a measurement: test sets, automatic metrics, and human evaluation protocols where metrics fall short. Run current models through it and show where they stand and where they break.
Define the datasets.
Specify the data that would teach models the missing behaviour: what to record, from whom, in which languages and conditions, and how to label it. Our operations team builds it to your spec, and you own its quality.
Train models on that data.
Train and fine-tune models on the new data to prove it works. You'll be responsible both for making the numbers go up and for making sure the numbers mean something. The bar: models that climb our evals, our leaderboards and other public leaderboards.
Publish and open-source.
Write up the problem, the eval, the data and the results, and release the models. We want this work to be cited and built on, not just shipped.

In a typical week, you might:
Listen to hundreds of model outputs to find a failure that no metric is catching yet
Write the spec for a new eval and review the first batch of test data with the operations team
Run training runs and ablations, and dig into results that don't quite make sense
Check a new model launch against our boards and explain what its scores really mean
Talk to researchers at labs about the problems they are stuck on
Write up results for a paper, a blog post or a leaderboard release

What matters most
Everything in the loop serves two outcomes. They are how this role will be measured.
1. Building the right evals

An eval only matters if climbing it means real progress. Many speech benchmarks saturate, or reward models that learn the test instead of the skill. You'll own making sure a better score on our evals means a model is genuinely closer to the frontier of voice AI and to machines that talk like humans. You should be able to say what an eval measures, what it misses, and how it could be gamed. In practice:
Start from behaviour.
Every eval begins with a behaviour we want models to have, not with a metric that happens to be easy to compute.
Check against people.
Validate that scores agree with what human listeners actually prefer, and use human evaluation where automatic metrics fall short.
Keep it hard to game.
Use held-out and refreshed test sets, watch for contamination, and retire an eval once it stops separating good models from great ones.
Cover real speech.
Test across languages, accents, code-mixing, noise and real conversation, not only clean, read English.
Be rigorous.
Report confidence intervals, and tell real effects apart from noise and bugs before calling a ranking.

2. Building the models

Evals tell the field where to go; models prove the path works. You'll train models on the data you defined and show that they climb, so the behaviours we set and the data we design are backed by results, not opinion. In practice:
Train and fine-tune.
Work with open ASR, TTS and speech to speech models, fine-tuning them on the datasets built to your spec.
Prove what caused the gain.
Run clean ablations against honest baselines, so the improvement is shown to come from the new data and behaviour, not from tuning to the test.
Climb public boards.
Move up our leaderboards and other existing ones, such as Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard, with results others can reproduce.
Train efficiently.
Keep training runs reproducible and make the most of every GPU hour.
Release openly.
Open-source the models with clear model cards, so labs and researchers can build on them.

What we offer
Hard, open problems.
Own the research questions that decide whether machines can talk like humans, across recognition, synthesis and conversation.
Open-source models.
Release the models you train, under your name.
Co-authorship on papers.
Co-author our papers at Interspeech, ICASSP and other top venues.
Real impact.
Your evals shape how labs build speech models and how the industry chooses between them.

Minimum qualifications
An MS or PhD in speech, ML or NLP, or an equivalent industry research
record
Strong Python and PyTorch,
and comfort with large audio datasets
Statistical care: you know when a ranking difference is real and when it is noise
Informed opinions about where voice AI is heading, not just familiarity with the tools
Solid engineering habits: version control, tests, reproducible experiments and pipelines others can run

new_jobs.title: Applied AI Architect, Security Specialist
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic’s Applied AI team helps the world’s largest organizations put Claude to work. As a Cybersecurity Specialist on Applied AI, you’ll be part of an overlay team of domain experts who sit alongside our enterprise account teams and bring deep security expertise to the accounts where it matters most.

You won’t own an account. You’ll be the security expert the account team pulls in to win and grow the most important security conversations: helping CISOs and security leaders see where Claude can take on real security work, then guiding them from early pilots to durable, production workloads. You’ll cover a portfolio of enterprise accounts across regulated industries like financial services, insurance, and healthcare, strategic accounts like semiconductors (IP protection, industrial control systems, export controls), and digital natives and public sector agencies, each with its own threat model.

How This Team Works

You partner with account executives, account architects, and generalist Applied AI engineers, who own the customer relationship and the broader technical engagement. You bring the security depth they don’t have time to build.
You work across many accounts at once, so the playbooks, reference implementations, and evaluation approaches you build are reused across the field, not just for one customer.
You are the connection point between the field and Anthropic’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams, turning what you see in customer security programs into product feedback.
You work alongside ISVs, systems integrators, and managed security providers who already serve these customers, enabling them where they own the engagement rather than competing with them.

Responsibilities

Join account teams to understand a customer’s security program, identify where Claude can do meaningful security work, and turn that into a technical plan and business case
Serve as the security-domain technical advisor on strategic enterprise accounts, from discovery through deployment
Move customers from one-time code scanning to sustained security workloads: application security in the SDLC, continuous automated penetration testing, alert triage and investigation, and threat intelligence that answers “does this new vulnerability affect us, and where”
Build and maintain reference implementations, harnesses, and evaluation approaches, and help customers adapt them to their own environments and controls
Run workshops and hands-on sessions where customer security teams use Claude on their own code and workflows
Equip partners to deliver Claude-powered security outcomes, with a clear line between what Anthropic delivers and what partners deliver
Speak credibly to every audience, from appsec engineers to CISOs and executives, including how to explain the value and risk of security work in business terms
Define and track adoption depth for each security workload across your accounts, and work with Product and Engineering on the telemetry to measure it
Write the playbooks and best practices the rest of the field can reuse, including how Claude complements the security tooling customers already own
Develop reference customers who can speak to the value they’re realizing
Stay current on frontier LLM capabilities and the new classes of vulnerabilities and attacks they surface
Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops and technical deep dives

You may be a good fit if you have

5+ years in security roles, with hands-on depth in at least two of: application security and secure SDLC, offensive security and penetration testing, detection and response, or threat intelligence and vulnerability management
Experience in a technical customer-facing role (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, security consultant, TAM), or on a security team where you had to win investment from leadership
Experience with large enterprise customers and complex, multi-stakeholder buying cycles, including working alongside the vendors and partners already in the account
The ability to translate between security teams, engineering teams, and executives
Comfort with Python, CI/CD, and cloud environments, plus hands-on experience using LLMs for security work such as code review, vulnerability discovery, triage, or investigation
A love of teaching and a collaborative approach to working across teams and balancing competing priorities

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$300,000—$400,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

new_jobs.title: Solution Architect (AWS-to-GCP Migration)
new_jobs.description:
Principal Solution Architect (AWS-to-GCP Migration)

Location:
Must be located in, or able to go to, the NY office on Mon, Tues, Wed, and Thurs
Duration:
Long-Term Contract

Position Overview:

We are seeking a Senior Principal Solution Architect
to provide end-to-end technical leadership for the migration of an Application Development Framework from AWS to Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

This is a highly visible architecture and delivery leadership role responsible for defining the GCP target architecture, establishing the foundational cloud infrastructure required to host and develop applications, translating business and technical requirements into executable solutions, and directing distributed engineering teams through implementation.

The architect will work closely with key business and technology stakeholders in New York and Chicago
, engineering and infrastructure teams, offshore delivery teams in India
, and the Program Management Office (PMO)
. The individual will be expected to operate across architecture, infrastructure, application development, security, DevOps, and program planning.

A critical aspect of this role is establishing the GCP landing zone and platform foundation required to support the Application Development Framework
, including networking, identity and access management, security, environments, compute, containerization, CI/CD, observability, secrets management, infrastructure-as-code, connectivity, and operational governance.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on enterprise cloud architect and technical leader
who can define the architecture, establish the infrastructure foundation, guide engineering teams, resolve complex technical issues, and help turn the overall migration strategy into an executable delivery plan.

Key Responsibilities:

1. AWS-to-GCP Migration Architecture:

• Own the end-to-end solution architecture for migrating the Application Development Framework from AWS to GCP.
• Assess the existing AWS application framework, infrastructure, services, integrations, security architecture, deployment processes, and operational model.
• Define the GCP target-state architecture and migration strategy.
• Develop AWS-to-GCP service mappings and determine where services should be:
Rehosted
Replatformed
Refactored
Re-engineered
Replaced with native GCP capabilities

2. GCP Infrastructure Foundation and Landing Zone:

• A major responsibility of this role will be to design and establish the GCP infrastructure foundation required to support enterprise-scale application development and deployment.
• The architect will define the infrastructure architecture required before and alongside migration of the Application Development Framework.
3. Application Platform Architecture:

Define the GCP platform services required to provide a scalable and reusable foundation for application development.
4. DevOps, CI/CD and Infrastructure-as-Code:

Define the engineering platform required to enable repeatable, automated deployment of the Application Development Framework and its applications.
5. Observability and Operational Readiness:

Design the operational architecture required to run the Application Development Framework reliably in GCP.
6. Application Environment Strategy:

Define how application development environments will be structured and managed across GCP.
7. Requirements Analysis and Solution Definition:

• Work directly with stakeholders in New York and Chicago to understand business objectives, technical requirements, constraints, and priorities.
• Lead requirements-gathering and discovery sessions.
• Translate business requirements into technical and architectural requirements.
• Define functional and non-functional requirements.
• Identify ambiguities and gaps and drive stakeholders toward resolution.
• Develop solution alternatives and clearly communicate architecture trade-offs.
• Maintain traceability between requirements, architecture decisions, technical deliverables, and implementation outcomes.
8. Technical Leadership of Offshore Delivery:

• Provide technical leadership and direction to offshore engineering and infrastructure teams in India.
• Translate architecture into actionable technical work packages.
• Establish implementation standards, acceptance criteria, architectural guardrails, and engineering patterns.
• Review technical designs and implementation approaches produced by offshore teams.
• Conduct regular architecture and technical working sessions.
• Resolve technical questions and architectural blockers.
• Ensure offshore teams have sufficient documentation and context to execute effectively.
• Coordinate work across application, infrastructure, DevOps, security, networking, and data engineering teams.
• Establish clear ownership and accountability for technical deliverables.
9. Program Planning and PMO Partnership:

The architect will work closely with the Program Management Office to translate the technical strategy into an executable migration program.
10. Stakeholder Management:

• Serve as the senior technical architecture liaison across New York, Chicago, India, and other participating teams.
• Build relationships with business leaders, product owners, application leaders, infrastructure teams, security teams, DevOps teams, engineering managers, and PMO leadership.
• Facilitate architecture and decision-making forums.
• Resolve conflicting priorities and drive stakeholder alignment.
• Communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and executive audiences.
• Present architecture options, risks, recommendations, and decisions to senior leadership.

Required Qualifications:

• 15+ years of experience
in solution architecture, enterprise architecture, cloud architecture, or related technology leadership roles.
• Significant experience leading large-scale cloud migration and modernization programs.

• Strong expertise in both AWS and GCP
, with demonstrated ability to design enterprise-scale cloud architectures.
• Proven experience migrating applications or platforms from AWS to GCP.
• Experience establishing enterprise GCP landing zones and cloud foundations.

• Experience designing infrastructure platforms that support multiple application development teams.
• Strong requirements analysis and technical documentation skills.
• Experience leading distributed teams across the US and India.

• Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
• Experience working closely with PMOs on complex technology programs.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect certification or equivalent expertise.
• AWS Solutions Architect certification or equivalent expertise.
• Strong Terraform experience.
• Experience with GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud Load Balancing, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, and related GCP services.
• Experience with Kubernetes and container orchestration.
• Experience with enterprise API management and microservices.
• Experience with DevSecOps and automated infrastructure provisioning.
• Experience with cloud financial management and cost optimization.
• Experience in regulated or large enterprise environments.
• Experience establishing reusable internal developer platforms or Platform Engineering
capabilities.

Overall Role Mandate

The Senior Principal Solution Architect will own the technical vision and execution direction for the Application Development Framework's transition to GCP.

The role goes beyond application migration. The architect will establish the GCP cloud foundation, infrastructure, security, networking, DevOps, platform services, and operational capabilities necessary to make GCP the strategic home for the Application Development Framework and the applications built upon it.

The successful candidate will therefore need to be equally comfortable defining an enterprise architecture, designing a GCP landing zone, whiteboarding an application platform, reviewing Terraform and CI/CD designs, leading technical workshops, directing offshore engineering teams, resolving stakeholder conflicts, and helping the PMO turn the technical strategy into a detailed execution plan.

new_jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Applied AI
new_jobs.description:
Join Tech @ Ro to build the future of healthcare, from the ground up!

At Ro, we believe that when people achieve their health goals, they can achieve their life goals. The highest-leverage way to move society forward is to give people their health, and the current healthcare system isn’t built to do that. It was built to bill, not to serve patients.

We’re building a new system. One where the patient is in control. One designed from scratch for the digital age.

At Ro, technology isn’t just a function… It's core to how we deliver care .
We’ve built a vertically integrated healthcare platform that connects telehealth, diagnostics, pharmacy, and logistics into a seamless, end-to-end experience for millions of patients.

…and we’re just getting started.

As part of Tech @ Ro , you’ll work on systems that operate at scale, with an opportunity to:

Solve complex, high-concurrency problems across a full-stack platform
Build and ship quickly with tight feedback loops and real-world impact
Own systems end-to-end, from architecture to production performance
Work alongside experienced operators, technical leaders, and clinicians
Help define how modern healthcare should be delivered

We’re a performance-driven team with a strong sense of ownership and urgency. We move fast, learn quickly, and hold a high bar for what we build, and do so with a big heart — because patients depend on it.

If you’re motivated by impact, scale, and the chance to help lead the patient revolution, come build with us.

The Role

Ro is building a team focused on shipping LLM-powered products across the patient experience, clinical operations, and internal tooling.

We're hiring a Senior Engineer, Applied AI to join a new team we’re building from the ground up alongside a Senior AI Lead and an Engineering Manager. You'll own AI features from prototype through production and spend as much time improving workflows with clinical operators as writing code. Most of your work will involve building orchestration layers, prompts, evaluations, retrieval systems, and tooling that make LLMs reliable enough for real-world healthcare operations.

What You'll Do

Design, build, and ship production LLM powered features end-to-end.
Build the AI application layer, including prompt orchestration, tool calling, retrieval (RAG), embeddings, agent workflows, and structured outputs.
Develop evaluation infrastructure, including regression suites, LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, synthetic datasets, human review workflows, and quality metrics that catch regressions before users do.
Design observability systems that measure accuracy, latency, cost, hallucination rates, and model behavior in production.
Build safety and reliability guardrails that ensure AI systems meet quality, compliance, and operational requirements.
Evaluate and integrate third-party tools, including orchestration frameworks, evaluation platforms, vector databases, and model providers; and make pragmatic build-versus-buy decisions.
Raise engineering standards across the team through technical leadership, code reviews, mentorship, and thoughtful system design.
Sit with EHR operators, Patient Advocates, and clinical teams to understand the workflows you're automating.
Prototype quickly, ship early, measure outcomes, and iterate based on real-world usage.

What You’ll Bring To The Team

5+ years building production software, with at least 1–2 years building and deploying LLM-powered applications in production (or equivalent depth through substantial side projects or open-source work).
Strong Python engineer with experience building backend services and integrating modern AI APIs and frameworks.
Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools throughout the software development lifecycle.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, ML Training Performance
new_jobs.description:
Zoox is on a mission to reimagine transportation and ground-up build autonomous robotaxis that are safe, reliable, clean, and enjoyable for everyone. We are still in the early stages of deploying our robotaxis on public roads, and it is a great time to join Zoox and have a significant impact in executing this mission. The ML Platform team at Zoox plays a crucial role in enabling innovations in large-scale Foundation models, VLMs, and VLAs to make autonomous driving as seamless as possible.

The Opportunity

Are you excited to drive our ML Training Performance initiatives and make the models that power autonomous driving trains faster, cheaper, and at greater scale? You will work with SOTA accelerators and cutting-edge techniques in distributed training, parallelism strategies, mixed-precision training and RL, especially for VLA and VLM models that are multi-modal — partnering closely with all the Autonomy teams within Zoox (Perception, Prediction, Planner, Simulation, Collision Avoidance) and pushing the boundaries of how ML training is practiced at Zoox.

We build and operate the base layer of ML tools, model development, and training systems that our applied research teams use for in- and off-vehicle ML use cases. You will work alongside a team of strong software engineers and act as a force multiplier for our internal customers. This team has many growth opportunities as we expand our robotaxi deployments and venture into new ML domains. If you want to learn more about our stack behind autonomous driving, please look here . If you want to learn more about our ML Infrastructure, here is one of our past talks at re:Invent.

In This Role, You Will

Design, implement, and operate cutting-edge ML training performance optimization techniques — distributed training (data/tensor/pipeline parallelism), mixed-precision, gradient checkpointing, and GPU kernels — to scale our VLM, VLA, and Foundational models training efficiency.
Work on RL framework and RL performance optimization for driving foundation model
Profile and debug training throughput bottlenecks across the compute, compiler, framework, and cluster-networking stack.
Collaborate closely with ML researchers, data engineers, and hardware engineers to define requirements and align on architectural decisions for large-scale training infrastructure.
Implement custom kernels and build benchmarks to track and validate training-performance optimizations across the stack.

Qualifications

Note: You do not have to meet all the requirements below to be considered for this position:

4+ years of total experience, including 2+ years working on large-scale model training platforms.
Experience with distributed training frameworks (Megatron-LM, TorchTitan), efficiently utilizing GPU/accelerator clusters at scale.
Experience with RL framework such as Verl/MILES and RL algorithms(GRPO, PPO)
Experience with collective communication libraries (e.g., NCCL) and optimizing communication/compute overlap in multi-node training.
Experience using profiling tools (NVIDIA Nsight, PyTorch Profiler, or XLA/JAX profiling) to identify and resolve training bottlenecks.
Proficient in Python or C++.
Experience with ML compilers, performance tooling, or hardware/software co-design (e.g., GPU/TPU/accelerator architectures).

$177,000 - $270,000 a year

Base Salary Range

There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.

Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

About Zoox

Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

Follow us on LinkedIn

Accommodations

If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to [email protected] or your assigned recruiter.

A Final Note

You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Zoox, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.

new_jobs.title: Research Scientist, Legal Innovation through Frontier Technology Lab (liftlab), Stanford Law School
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Research Scientist, Legal Innovation through Frontier Technology Lab (liftlab), Stanford Law School

Budgeted Salary Range Upon Hire at the Law School: $117,000-$130,000 annual base salary.

Stanford’s liftlab seeks to increase access to high quality legal services in the private sector by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) and other frontier technologies. We design, investigate and evaluate AI tools in legal education and private practice that are aimed to both reduce the cost and increase the quality of legal services in a sustainable and responsible way. To bridge the gap between theory and practice, our work extends beyond conceptualization and encompasses the building of prototypes that help explore the utility of AI-based solutions. We are currently seeking a Research Scientist to join our team who will report directly to the Lab Directors.

As a Research Scientist You Will

In partnership with the Directors and other staff, execute and administer research activities on AI and other legal technological developments; make recommendations on project development and implementation.
Train classifiers, design/construct the architecture of AI platforms, build large language models (LLM) agents
Oversee and support training of research assistants and student fellows on best practices and technical skills.
Write and edit content for a variety of work product outputs, including peer-reviewed journal articles, white papers, project proposals, etc. Assist with the development of research grants, (i.e., may suggest new funding opportunities, write portions of grants, and/or summarize data for grant support).
Represent the Lab and the specific projects for which the Research Scientist is responsible or is assisting in leading as the key contact and subject matter expert and develop communications for internal and external constituencies.
Organize and/or participate in outreach activities such as events, partnerships, training, and conferences.
May assist in the teaching and administration of courses at the intersection of AI & Law.
Create and/or advise in the development of curriculum. Make recommendations for course improvements.

Core Duties

Leveraging state-of-the-art large language models, administer research activities.
Evaluate and develop new of modifications of usable data from complex data sources.
Assess and produce relevant, standard, or custom information from structured data sources by querying data repositories and generating the associated information.
Devise methods for identifying patterns and trends in valuable sources using software engineering principles and strong knowledge of at least programming language, such as Python or R; basic statistical ability. Determine and recommend additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and disseminate reports, academic articles and law reviews to contribute to the body of emerging scholarship in the space of law and AI.
Provide technical direction to other research staff and students.
Identify and select usable data from subtle and complex data patterns to find ways to train LLMs on experiential knowledge. Use principles of engineering and related fields (linguistics, data science, natural sciences, statistics, etc.),
Design methods to validate data to ensure high-quality output.
Evaluate existing tools and develop new prototypes of technological solutions to legal problems to ensure research translates into meaningful improvements in legal service accessibility and quality.

Nice To Have

Interest in the causal inference and social sciences, particularly law (although the relevant legal knowledge can be obtained on the job)

This position will be a two-year fixed-term appointment, subject to renewal.

To be considered, please submit the following items along with your online application:

CV
Include as part of your cover letter, project and code samples or GitHub
You may be asked to provide your transcript

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Evaluate and develop new or modifications of usable data from complex data sources. Assess and produce relevant, standard, or custom information (reports, charts, graphs, and tables) from structured data sources by querying data repositories and generating the associated information.
Devise methods for identifying patterns and trends in available information sources using a variety of qualitative and quantitative techniques. Determine and recommend additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and customize reports based on data in the database. Distribute and disseminate reports to applicable agencies, researchers, management, and other internal end-users.
Create non-routine databases and generate related information summaries.
Perform statistical analyses appropriate to complex data and reporting requirements.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics or surveys.
Lead the implementation of data standards and common data elements for data collection.
Collaborate with technical staff to standardize and systemize routine reports, dashboards, and metrics.
May test prototype software and participate in the approval and release process for new software.

Minimum Education

Bachelor’s degree.

Minimum Experience

Three years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience. Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics, or engineering.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

In-depth knowledge and experience using and applying analytical software, database management system software, database reporting software, database user interface and query software, and data mining software.
Demonstrated ability to collect data using a variety of methods, such as data mining and hardcopy or electronic documentation study, to improve or expand databases.
Intermediate statistical ability.
Strong listening, verbal, and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple activities in a deadline-oriented environment; highly organized, flexible, and rigorous attention to detail.
Ability to use logic to calculate data; efficiently construct a database or scrutinize the form of a question.
Ability to work with data of varying levels of quality and validity.
Demonstrated ability to produce data in a clear and understandable manner meeting user requirements.
Ability to work effectively with multiple internal and external customers.
Ability to take a leadership role on projects and with users/clients.
